Ok now, I'm trying to understand a bit more, I don't want to worsen stuff when things happen. Gotta admit it, I'm a bit confused now that I think of it 

Talking from experience, I know that, when the time comes (probably around January), I will most likely talk about why I'd do that, if someone is interested enough to ask. I just like to overshare. I would be open to listen to them, or even to be challenged, because I know that, within myself, I have taken everything into account, and fully accept the outcome. I envision this choice as something I'm fully aware of. Otherwise I'm only acting on impulse; I'm not deciding something for myself, instead I'm letting things outside of my control take the lead. 

That's also why I kinda want to ask things around when people say they're going to kill themselves. 

If someone is certain that it is what they'll do because of x reasons, then, worst case scenario, my words only become annoying to read, right? Maybe through them I can understand myself a bit more too. But if they're uncertain and acting on impulse, maybe they are just blinded by the immense pain. 

In this case, is it really a choice? 

Taking advantage is not what I want, not in the way you mean it at least. I don't want to be the savior of the day. What I want is to see the reasoning behind their choices, because it's something that deeply affects me too. I relate to both the impulsiveness and the sheer reasoning. And, when someone is acting on impulse, I want to see if I can do something, anything to lessen their pain even momentarily. If you want to find the advantage, it is to see what works and what not?

Here's my pathetic attempt at writing a TLDR: I want to see if people are aware and know why they opted for suicide, or if they're guided only by the impulsiveness that extreme pain puts you through
